key_insight: A variance-preserving denoising diffusion bridge model predicts stochastic Al–Cu solidification while retaining fine dendritic structure and running approximately 73× faster than the phase-field solver.
engineering_relevance: Faster microstructure prediction could enable broader process-condition screening and ensemble studies of rapid alloy solidification.
method: Condition VP-DDBM on current phase, Cu concentration, and prescribed temperature fields.
Predict the next two-dimensional phase and concentration state.
Apply predictions autoregressively to generate long rollouts.
evidence_signal: Across two held-out thermal gradients, VP-DDBM achieved lower long-horizon errors than deterministic U-Net and SI-ConvNeXt baselines in mean phase, mean Cu concentration, and leading-tip position.
watch_item: Validation is limited to two-dimensional simulations and two held-out thermal gradients; broader process and three-dimensional generalization remain unestablished.
paper_title: Surrogate Models for Stochastic Al-Cu Phase-Field Solidification
